title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-12
notes:
West leads the ♥Q against 4♠. West's heart opening lead is won in the dummy.

West's opening bid marks him with most of the outstanding high cards (certainly the ♠A and ♣AQ). South will have to lose at least those two Aces and a trump trick so he should play to minimize his chances of having to lose a 2nd club trick as well.

As long as South is able to keep East off lead, the ♣K will be safe from attack. Eventually, dummy's diamonds can be used to discard South's club losers, but South must draw trump first. South doesn't mind losing 2 trump tricks as long as West wins both of those tricks.

South should lead a trump from dummy at trick 2. If East follows with the ♠4, South should follow with a low spade from his hand, allowing West to win the trick cheaply. West can do no better than return a heart to the dummy. South can continue trump, playing an honor from his hand to force West's ♠A. West might as well cash the ♣A at this point to prevent an overtrick (as South is now in a position to draw East's last trump and run the diamonds).

If East plays the ♠9, ♠10, or ♠J on the first round of trump, South must cover with the ♠K or ♠Q to force West's ♠A. West returns a heart to the dummy and East follows with the ♠4 on the second round of trump. South should play a low spade on this trick to make sure that West wins the second trump trick for the defense. As before, West must cash the ♣A to prevent an overtrick. Otherwise, South would be able to draw East's last trump and run diamonds to discard his clubs.
